faqs.question: What props and gear go into a Ghostface shoot?
faqs.answer: One Ghostface mask, a black hooded robe, black gloves, a landline or chunky cordless phone, one lamp and a torch. Add a phone on a tripod with a 10-second timer and you can shoot all 8 frames in about an hour at home.

faqs.question: How long does a Ghostface couple photoshoot take?
faqs.answer: Plan 45 to 60 minutes for 8 frames in a living room, or 30 to 40 minutes on a porch. Most of the time goes on moving the one lamp between frames, not on the poses.

faqs.question: Do I need a real landline phone for the shoot?
faqs.answer: No, but a corded phone gives you the best reveal shot, the cord stretched from the target's hand to Ghostface's glove. An old cordless handset or a retro-style phone works for every other frame.

faqs.question: Who should wear the mask, me or my partner?
faqs.answer: Whoever can stay still longer, because the masked partner acts with angles and holds poses for 2 seconds at a time. Swap halfway: frame 7 of the shot list is built around the role swap.

faqs.question: What should the person on the phone wear?
faqs.answer: A plain, light-coloured top so they separate from the black robe in low light. Avoid black, busy prints or anything with a logo, which pull the eye away from the phone and the mask.

faqs.question: Why does Ghostface tilt his head in photos?
faqs.answer: The mask has no expression, so the tilt is the only way it shows curiosity or menace. In a 2024 study, people named emotions correctly on 73.8% of masked faces against 85.7% unmasked, and Ghostface covers the whole face.

faqs.question: Can we do a Ghostface shoot outside at night?
faqs.answer: Only on private property, out of sight of the street, with the neighbours told first. Masked figures in public drew reports in nearly every US state during the 2016 clown sightings, and a prop knife makes a call to the police far more likely.

faqs.question: Is the Ghostface mask I can buy the same one used in Scream?
faqs.answer: The Scream films use Fun World's mask under licence, according to a February 2026 complaint filed by Spyglass and Paramount. Shop versions vary in material and detail, and the design's origin is disputed by the effects studio Alterian.

faqs.question: When should we do the Halloween photoshoot?
faqs.answer: A few evenings before the day, so the photos are edited by Halloween: Saturday 31 October 2026 or Sunday 31 October 2027. Shoot after dusk indoors, where one lamp controls all the light.

faqs.question: How do I send the photos to my partner privately?
faqs.answer: Put them in a Halloween card or page and add a password at publish; 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it. The premium page also lets you set an unlock time so the photos appear at midnight on the 31st.

# Ghostface Couple Photoshoot: 8-Frame Shot List and Mask Rules

A Ghostface couple photoshoot is a Scream-themed shoot where one partner wears the Ghostface mask and robe and the other answers the phone: it rings, the caller is closer than expected, the mask comes off and you both laugh. Plan 8 frames, an hour and a private location, and shoot vertical, because 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone (27,725 of 57,456 views). If the set is private, lock it; 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it.

Below: who owns the mask (a Fun World trademark and a 2026 copyright fight), an original shot list, acting opposite a blank face, where not to take a prop knife, and clean captions.

## What is a Ghostface couple photoshoot?

A Ghostface couple photoshoot is a staged set of couple photos built on the masked caller from the 1996 film Scream: one partner is the caller, the other the target on the phone. The joke is that the "killer" is the person you love, so the last frame is affectionate rather than frightening.

On TikTok and Instagram the format leans 90s: a corded or chunky cordless landline, direct flash, a lamp-lit living room. The costume is one mask and one robe, and the figure has stayed recognisable across seven Scream films since 1996 (as of October 2026).

## Who owns the Ghostface mask, and can you post your photos?

Easter Unlimited, Inc., trading as Fun World, holds US trademark registration 4,256,208 for a stylised "Ghost Face" design (a cloaked ghost above the words), dated 11 December 2012 in the court record, and a copyright registration for the "Ghost Face" Mask with Shroud effective 23 February 1993, per a [27 September 2021 federal court ruling](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nyed.425540/gov.uscourts.nyed.425540.60.0.pdf). In that case Fun World sued NBA player Terry Rozier over "Scary Terry" T-shirts and hoodies and lost: the judge found fair use and granted him summary judgment on every claim.

The design's origin is disputed. A [February 2026 complaint by Spyglass and Paramount](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.cacd.1005650/gov.uscourts.cacd.1005650.1.0.pdf) says Fun World has licensed the mask to every Scream film, while the effects studio Alterian says its early-1990s "Wailer" mask came first; Fun World says it created its own independently in early 1991. Both 2026 suits closed on 12 May 2026, per the [federal court docket](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/72246018/the-alterian-ghost-factory-inc-v-easter-unlimited-inc/), with no public ruling on who designed it first.

For a couple, notice what all three cases were about: films, clothing and money. Selling prints, merchandise or paid "Ghostface sessions" is where the claims sat; this is a reading of court records, not legal advice.

## An 8-frame Ghostface call shot list

Shoot the frames in order, because they tell one story. Every frame lists action, light, camera and its job in the plot.

### 1. The first ring

- **Action:** the target answers on the sofa, knees up; Ghostface stands soft-focus in a doorway 3 metres behind.
- **Light:** one warm lamp by the target, doorway dark.
- **Camera:** 1x lens, portrait mode off so the figure stays readable.
- **Story job:** sets the room you will reuse in frame 7.

### 2. Unknown number

- **Action:** close-up of the handset, thumb over the answer key, masking tape on it reading "UNKNOWN".
- **Light:** a torch bounced off a white wall.
- **Camera:** 2x lens, exposure dragged down one stop.
- **Story job:** the hook that makes people swipe on.

### 3. Two ends of one call

- **Action:** the target on the landline indoors; Ghostface on the porch with a second phone, head tilted.
- **Light:** warm inside, cool porch bulb outside.
- **Camera:** same height and framing for both, posted as a diptych.
- **Story job:** shows the caller is close.

### 4. The cord gives it away

- **Action:** a curly cord runs from the target's hand to Ghostface's glove at the frame edge.
- **Light:** one side light so the coil throws a shadow.
- **Camera:** 0.5x lens low to the floor, cord corner to corner.
- **Story job:** the reveal that the caller is in the house.

### 5. In the TV screen

- **Action:** the target faces a switched-off TV; a white mask shows in the reflection.
- **Light:** room dim, one lamp behind the camera.
- **Camera:** focus on the reflection, not the target's back.
- **Story job:** the scare the viewer sees before the target does.

### 6. The tilt

- **Action:** Ghostface tilts the head 30 degrees and holds; the target freezes, receiver still up.
- **Light:** torch under the target's chin, mask lit from the side.
- **Camera:** 2 seconds of burst mode; keep the fullest tilt.
- **Story job:** peak tension.

### 7. Role swap

- **Action:** the target now wears the mask; the former Ghostface, hood down, holds the phone.
- **Light:** frame 1's lamp again.
- **Camera:** frame 1's angle exactly.
- **Story job:** the twist.

### 8. The unmasking

- **Action:** mask pushed up, foreheads close, phone dangling on its cord, both laughing.
- **Light:** ceiling light on, the brightest frame of the set.
- **Camera:** 10-second timer, 3 shots; the second is usually least stiff.
- **Story job:** the release.

Why end on a laugh: a [2024 paper in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10725765) proposes a horror "sweet spot" where fright and enjoyment meet, with anticipation, such as not knowing when the killer will strike, carrying most of the effect. Frames 1 to 6 build that anticipation; frame 8 resolves it.

## How do you act scared opposite a mask with no expression?

The masked partner cannot act with the face, so the body has to do it. In a [2024 Europe's Journal of Psychology study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10936662) of 50 adults aged 19 to 28, people named emotions correctly on 85.7% of unmasked faces and 73.8% of masked ones, and that was with the eyes still showing; Ghostface hides the lot. Three rules follow from that:

- **Ghostface acts with angles.** A head tilt, a lean through a doorway, one gloved hand on a frame; change one thing per shot.
- **The target carries the emotion.** Eyes wide, receiver in both hands, shoulders up. Ask for a gasp, not a scream; open mouths read as yawns in stills.
- **Shoot in bursts.** Take 10 frames per shot; movement beats a held pose.

## Four Ghostface shoot setups compared

Here are four locations for the shot list, set against light, time and risk. The living room wins for most couples.

| Setup | Light you need | Time for all 8 frames | Public-alarm risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Living room with a landline | 1 lamp, 1 torch | 45–60 min | None (private) |
| Porch or front door | Porch bulb after dusk | 30–40 min | Low; neighbours can see |
| Parked car at night | Dome light, phone torch | 30 min | Medium; a masked figure by a car alarms passers-by |
| Hired studio with 90s set | Studio strobes | 60 min booked slot | None; ask the studio about mask and prop rules first |

The car is the one setup where a stranger sees a masked figure with no context. Pick the living room unless you have a quiet private driveway.

## Masks and prop knives in public: where not to shoot

A masked figure in the wrong place can bring the police. During the [2016 clown sightings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_clown_sightings), people in clown masks near forests, schools and neighbourhoods were reported in nearly every US state, strained police resources in the UK and led to at least 12 US arrests, and school districts in California, New Jersey and Ohio banned clown masks outright. You mean no harm, but a passer-by sees only the mask.

- **Leave the prop knife out.** A phone in the glove reads as Ghostface and is creepier anyway.
- **Mask on only on private property.** Carry it to the spot in a bag.
- **Never near schools, playgrounds, car parks or shops.**
- **Text the neighbours before a porch shoot.** One line saves a 911 or 999 call.

## Captions, plus a Halloween card for your finished set

The trend has an NSFW side online; these lines stay clean, because your partner may show their mum. Every caption is original.

- He called. I picked up. Worst decision, best photos.
- Unknown caller, very known boyfriend.
- Some couples share a playlist. We share a landline.
- Caller ID said "trouble". I answered anyway.
- Line busy every 31 October.
- Screening every call except hers.
- Plot twist: the masked one does the dishes.
- Never says a word in the photos. Still the funniest person I know.

An Instagram post and a private set sent with a note land differently. The [Halloween card that carries six of your frames](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) fits frames 1, 4, 6 and 8; it is a five-minute build, and your partner clears fog from haunted portraits to reveal each shot, then finds your letter waiting in a dark attic. For the whole set with your voice on it, the [premium Halloween page where a spirit radio plays your 60-second recording](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) fits 12 photos, is a ten-minute build, and can sit behind a countdown until an unlock time you pick, such as midnight on Saturday 31 October 2026 or Sunday 31 October 2027.

Shared SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, so plan for repeat visits. Not shot yet? Send [a date invite that needs a reply](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation); it turns "shoot with me on the 30th?" into a yes and a countdown.

## When a Ghostface couple shoot is the wrong plan

Drop the idea if your partner dislikes horror or masks; a theme one person tolerates shows in every frame. Skip it if the only location is public, and skip the robe-and-knife look around children.

SubhSandesh loses too. If you want prints on the wall, order prints; a page is a link, opened on a phone 48.3% of the time. Both pages are in English and meant for one recipient, never a friend group's gallery, and anyone selling Ghostface sessions needs a lawyer, not a card.

## Sources

- Easter Unlimited, Inc. v. Rozier, E.D.N.Y. No. 18-CV-06637, order of 27 September 2021.
- Spyglass Media Group v. The Alterian Ghost Factory, C.D. Cal. No. 2:26-cv-01235, complaint of 6 February 2026.
- The Alterian Ghost Factory v. Easter Unlimited, C.D. Cal. No. 2:26-cv-01260, docket, closed 12 May 2026.
- Miller, White and Scrivner, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 2024.
- Hysenaj et al., Europe's Journal of Psychology, February 2024.
- Wikipedia, "2016 clown sightings".
